resources.string: One UI gives apps no way to set the sizes of three split-screen panes. When you open a MultiTasker shortcut with custom sizes, this service drags the split-screen dividers to those sizes, like you would with your finger.\n\nIt only performs those drags, right after a shortcut opens. It does not read what is on your screen and does not see what you type.

To size three apps, turn on \"%1$s\" in Accessibility. One UI has no setting for this, so MultiTasker drags the dividers into place after opening the apps. It doesn\'t read your screen.

Android only lets apps open two apps side by side, at equal size. For a real third split pane and custom sizes, grant two permissions once over ADB from a computer (or a wireless-debugging app on the phone):
Existing 3-app shortcuts switch to 3-way split as soon as the grant is in place. Uninstalling the app removes the grant.

Some apps, like Instagram, keep their old layout after their first resize when they had to start from scratch. This drags their dividers a second time. Only when an app wasn\'t already running; adds about a second.
